newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: POSCO aims for hefty capacity increase.
newsitem.headline: POSCO aims for hefty capacity increase.

text.p: South Korea's largest steel maker Pohang Iron and Steel Co Ltd (POSCO) said on Tuesday its new Kwanguang No.5 blast furnace will have annual capacity of 3.0 million tonnes when completed in 1998.

A POSCO spokesman said the company will invest 409.6 billion won in the Kwangyang No.5 blast furnace, scheduled for completion by September 1998. POSCO held a ground-breaking ceremony for the furnace on Tuesday.
The No.5 blast furnace will start operation by 1999 and make POSCO the world's largest steel maker with total production capacity of 28 million tonnes.
The spokesman said POSCO planned to build a No.2 mini-mill with production capacity of two million tonnes by February 1999 soon after the No.5 blast furnace begins production.
The spokesman said in a statement the Kwangyang No.1 mini-mill had also started operation with annual production capacity of 1.8 million tonnes.
With the completion of the No.1 mini-mill, POSCO's total steel production will be increased to 26 million tonnes by 1997 from a current 23 million tonnes, the spokesman said.

In addition to POSCO's expansion with the No.5 blast furnace, other Korean steel makers will continue their facility expansion increasing South Korea's total production volume to 52 million tonnes by 1999 from 37 million tonnes in 1996.
That expansion will rank South Korea as the world's fourth largest steel producer after the United States, Japan and China, POSCO said. Currently South Korea is the fifth largest producer.
South Korea's per capita steel consumption and per capita crude steel production will be 885 kilogrammes and 1,100 kilogrammes respectively by early 2000.
